In this section, we will see how some of the ideas we learned in earlier sections can look in data analysis. Feel free to follow along with the code using R on your own machine.

## Epidemiological Model : SIR

To start, we can set up an example of what an SIR model might look like in the population and change around parameters to see what happens.

Credit for this tutorial goes to the MIDAS-CCDD Outreach Conference on March 4th 2024, adapted from material from Professor Mathew Kiang and Dr.Stephen Kissler.

### Preliminaries

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Install deSolve package (will only need to be done once)
install.packages("deSolve", dep = TRUE)
```

```{r warning= FALSE}
library(deSolve)
```


The `deSolve` package will help us with the math behind the SIR model example.

### Setting up the SIR model

```{r}
dt <- seq(from = 1 , to= 365 , by= 1)
```
